question: Why do vectors like [1, 1] usually fail to be eigenvectors for a diagonal scaling matrix?
direct_answer: Because the transformation changes their components by different amounts, so the direction usually changes.
expanded_answer: If one coordinate is stretched more than the other, a diagonal vector such as [1, 1] typically gets bent to a new direction rather than staying on the same line. Only special directions aligned with the scaling axes remain unchanged as directions.
key_points: Eigenvectors must keep the same line through the origin
common_wrong_ideas: Thinking any vector in 2D will be preserved by a scaling matrix
Confusing component-wise scaling with directional preservation
